archetype.name: Playoff Team (shooting-first)
archetype.definition: A top-ten outfit whose offense, powered by Curry and the league's best three-point shooting, carries a middling defense and a thin frontcourt, good enough to win most nights but not yet built to beat the elite.

report.headline: Honest 8-5 built on Curry and league-best shooting, now tested without him
report.take:
A year after a 37-45 season that ranked 20th on the site, Golden State is 8-5 and eighth, and the record is not a mirage. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0, and the margin implies exactly the 8 wins it has. The Net Rtg of 4.3 ranks 11th. That comes from an offense eighth in the league at 117.7 points per 100 possessions and a defense 12th at 113.4. Most of it is the shooting: a league-best 3P % of 39.4 on a diet where 47.8% of the shots come from deep. This is a perimeter team in the purest sense.

The engine is Stephen Curry. His BPM is 14.2, his TS % is 71.9, the team is 16 points per 100 better with him on the floor, and he sits second of 86 on the point guard tab. Around him the backcourt grades B+ and the wings A-. The wing grade leans almost entirely on Yaxel Lendeborg's volume: 263 points on a 26.7 USG %. His On-Off of -32.3 is a flag worth watching, even allowing for a small sample. The frontcourt grades F. Draymond Green is a passer now (78 assists against a 45.4 TS %), and Al Horford is shooting 48.5 TS %. The one big who has moved the needle, Charles Bassey (71 TS %, On-Off 16.8), has played only 146 minutes.

Two things in the profile deserve skepticism. The 3P % is above anything in this franchise's recent history; the best of the last five seasons was 38.5 and last year's was 35.6, so some of the shooting will cool. The defense also has a split personality. It keeps opponents out of the paint better than almost anyone (Opp Rim Rate 24.5, 3rd), a real change from last year's 29.1. But when teams get there they finish at 70.1%, 28th. That is the F frontcourt showing up. November's defense was sharper than October's, allowing 109.86 a game against 115.33, which makes the improvement look partly real.

The immediate problem is that Curry is listed Out, and he has played only 10 of the 13 games. The run that defined the start, an eight-game winning streak, ended with a loss at Houston and an 85-123 beating at San Antonio. The sheet doesn't say who played in those games, but the drop-off fits what his On-Off implies. Over a full season this team looks like a mid-40s-win playoff side. How long Curry is out decides whether it stays in the top eight or slides toward the play-in pack.

strengths.title: League's best three-point shooting
strengths.body: Golden State hits 39.4% from three, first in the league and well above the league average, while taking 47.8% of its shots from deep. That volume-plus-accuracy combination is why the offense ranks eighth despite an F frontcourt. Expect some cooling, since it is beyond any of the last five seasons. The shot profile itself is sustainable.

strengths.title: Curry is still a superstar
strengths.body: Curry's BPM of 14.2 and 71.9 TS % on a 34 USG % are elite by any standard. The team is 16 points per 100 better with him on the floor. He is the reason a roster with an F frontcourt has a top-ten offense. The production lasts as long as he is healthy, and right now he is not.

strengths.title: A record that matches the margin
strengths.body: Nothing here is propped up by close-game luck. W vs Pt Diff is 0 and the margin implies all 8 wins, and the last ten games produced a +9 differential a game. The defense also tightened in November, allowing 109.86 a game. The 8-5 is earned.

concerns.title: Curry is out
concerns.body: Curry has played 10 of 13 games and is listed Out. The last game, an 85-123 loss at San Antonio, is a reminder of how steep the fall can be without him. No other guard comes close to replacing his creation. Melton's On-Off is -11.3 and Will Richard's is -18.8.

concerns.title: No rim protection behind the scheme
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades F, and it shows at the basket. Opponents rarely get to the rim (24.5% of shots, 3rd), but they convert 70.1% when they do, 28th in the league. Green and Horford are both below 50 TS % on offense. Bassey is the only big with strong numbers, in limited minutes.

concerns.title: Small forwards feast on this defense
concerns.body: Opposing small forwards put up 5.84 more points, rebounds and assists combined than their usual, the worst mark in the league. Shooting guards also score heavily, at 29.38 points a game, 26th. The perimeter defense outside the point guard spot is leakier than the overall Def Rank of 12 suggests.

trend.note: A .500 October gave way to an eight-game winning streak built on a much tighter defense, then two road losses, the second a 38-point-style blowout at San Antonio. With Curry out, the near-term path is unclear.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games and Boston, with Curry out
weekAhead.body:
The week splits cleanly in two. The road trip opens at New Orleans, owners of the league's worst defense (121.2 DRtg, 30th) and an Opp eFG % of 57, 28th. Dallas follows: a 7-7, 18th-ranked side with a D frontcourt and below-average offense. Both are games a playoff team should win, even shorthanded.

The back half is a different story. Memphis comes the night after Dallas: 9-4, fifth in Net Rtg, a top-four offense and an A backcourt, on the second night of a back-to-back. Then site No. 1 Boston comes to the Bay at 11-2, with the league's best Net Rtg at 13.7 and the second-best defense. A 2-2 week without Curry would be par. Anything better says the supporting cast is real.

keyMatchups.title: Shooting into a broken New Orleans defense
keyMatchups.body: The Pelicans allow 121.2 points per 100 and let opponents shoot 71.4% at the rim, 29th. They also give up the most to power forwards of any team. That is a rare soft spot for Golden State's weak frontcourt, and its shooters should find room even without Curry.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis guards on a back-to-back
keyMatchups.body: Memphis brings an A backcourt and the league's second-best 3P % at 39.2. Golden State's defense allows shooting guards 29.38 points a game, 26th. With tired legs on the second night, this is the game most likely to get away.

keyMatchups.title: Boston's wings and rim defense
keyMatchups.body: Boston's A wings meet a defense that ranks last against small forwards relative to their norms. At the other end, Boston's opponents hit only 59.3% at the rim, second best, which removes the one easy source of points Golden State's bigs have. Without Curry, this is the hardest game on the schedule.

weekAhead.watch: Who soaks up Curry's shots: whether Lendeborg's volume and Podziemski's efficiency can keep the offense near its top-ten level against New Orleans and Dallas.

restOfSeason.body:
The season pace is 50 wins, and the underlying numbers support a real playoff team rather than a fluke. The record matches the margin, the offense is eighth and the defense is a tick above average. Two forces pull that pace down. The first is Curry's absence of unknown length, since everything about this roster runs through him. The second is a 3P % that is running above anything the franchise has posted in the last five years. I'd project something in the mid-40s for wins, with the shooting easing toward the high 37s and the Net Rtg settling a bit lower than it is now.

What should hold is the shot profile and the defense's ability to keep opponents off the rim, which marks a real shift from last season. What won't fix itself is the frontcourt. Unless Bassey's minutes grow and his numbers hold, size and finishing will cost this team against the best teams on its schedule, Boston and Memphis among them.
swingFactors: How far the three-point shooting cools
Whether Bassey earns a bigger frontcourt role

confidence.note: Thirteen games, and Curry's injury of unknown length clouds every projection.
